item.title: Bronny James Faces a Career Crossroads Without LeBron
item.description:
What happens to a 21-year-old NBA player when the reason he was drafted suddenly walks out the door?

That is the very real question facing Bronny James this summer. His father, LeBron James, is leaving the Los Angeles Lakers after eight seasons — and Bronny’s carefully guarded roster spot has never looked more fragile.

Quick Summary

  • Bronny James’ $2.3 million contract for 2026-27 was fully guaranteed by the Lakers.
  • LeBron James is leaving the Lakers in free agency, reshaping his son’s outlook.
  • A recent Deandre Ayton trade signals Bronny will likely be dealt to LeBron’s next team.
  • One Fox Sports analyst even suggested Bronny should retire after two seasons.

Why Bronny James’ Lakers Future Suddenly Matters

Bronny James entered the league as a former second-round pick out of USC, and the storyline was always about family. Playing alongside his Hall of Fame father was historic — the first father-son duo to share an NBA court.

item.title: Deandre Ayton's Stunning Playoff Reinvention
item.description:
What if the most important player in the Los Angeles Lakers’ first-round sweep attempt isn’t Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, or even LeBron James — but the center who openly bristled at being asked to play defense just months ago?

That’s the strange, fascinating story of Deandre Ayton right now. After a regular season where he averaged a quiet 12.5 points and 8 rebounds, Ayton has thrown himself into a defensive role he once resisted, and the Lakers have built a 3-0 lead over the Houston Rockets because of it.

item.title: Drew Timme's Surprising Rise: From Undrafted to Lakers Starter
item.description:
Drew Timme’s Surprising Rise: From Undrafted to Lakers Starter

Gonzaga’s all-time leading scorer couldn’t get drafted. Now Drew Timme is starting games for the Los Angeles Lakers — and making believers out of everyone who counted him out.

Key Takeaways:

  • Drew Timme signed a two-way contract with the Lakers in November 2025 after Deandre Ayton’s injury
  • The 25-year-old averaged 25.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 4.0 assists with the South Bay Lakers in the G League
  • As Gonzaga’s all-time leading scorer (2,307 points), Timme went undrafted in 2023 before grinding through the G League
  • He’s now earning starts for the Lakers, including an April 8 matchup against OKC

From March Madness Star to Undrafted Free Agent

Drew Timme wasn’t supposed to end up here. At Gonzaga, the 6-foot-10 big man was a three-time All-American and two-time West Coast Conference Player of the Year. He left as the program’s all-time leading scorer with 2,307 points across four seasons — a resume that screams NBA lottery pick in most eras.

item.title: Luka Doncic Stats Are Rewriting Lakers History — Here's the Proof
item.description:
Has any player in the NBA right now been more unstoppable than Luka Doncic? The Los Angeles Lakers guard just dropped 60 points against the Miami Heat on March 20, extending the Lakers’ winning streak to seven games — and his individual numbers over this stretch are borderline absurd.

Key Takeaways:

  • Doncic scored 60 points in Miami, his latest masterpiece during a scorching hot run
  • He has scored at least 30 points in seven consecutive games
  • Season averages entering the Rockets game: 32.9 PPG, 7.9 RPG, 8.5 APG, 1.5 SPG on 47.4% shooting
  • Doncic became the youngest player in NBA history to reach 1,600 career three-pointers
  • The Lakers have climbed to the third seed in the Western Conference

Luka Doncic Stats During the Seven-Game Win Streak

The numbers alone tell a staggering story. Doncic has scored at least 30 points in every single game during the Lakers’ current seven-game winning streak, a run that has vaulted Los Angeles into serious contention as the third seed in the West.
